question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle 1 - 2 x,y,- 2 z\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v + 1,u,v\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
0\le u\le 2,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle 1,-1,-1\rangle.
$$

You may use

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle 1,-1,-1\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u + v + 1,\quad y=u,\quad z=v.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - 2 u - 2 v - 1,u,- 2 v\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- 2 u - 2 v - 1)(1) \\ &=- 2 u- 2 v \\ &\quad {}-1 \\ T_{2}&=(u)(-1) \\ &=- u \\ T_{3}&=(- 2 v)(-1) \\ &=2 v\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=- 3 u-1\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=- 3 u v- v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=- 6 u-2\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=- 3 u^{2}- 2 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{0}^{2}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=0}^{u=2} \\ &=-16.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle 6 y z,- x,3\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 1 - 2 u,u v^{2},-1\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
2\le u\le 4,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u$. Enter an exact value.

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Differentiate the parametrization:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle -2,v^{2},0\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,2 u v,0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k \\ -2&v^{2}&0 \\ 0&2 u v&0\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\langle 0,0,- 4 u v\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Reverse its sign for the specified order:

$$
\mathbf N=-\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle 0,0,4 u v\rangle.
$$

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=1 - 2 u,\quad y=u v^{2},\quad z=-1.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - 6 u v^{2},2 u - 1,3\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- 6 u v^{2})(0) \\ &=0 \\ T_{2}&=(2 u - 1)(0) \\ &=0 \\ T_{3}&=(3)(4 u v) \\ &=12 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=12 u v\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=6 u v^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=48 u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=24 u^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{2}^{4}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=2}^{u=4} \\ &=288.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle -3,3 y,2 z^{2}\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle - v,3 u v,u\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
0\le u\le 2,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle - 3 u,-1,3 v\rangle.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle - 3 u,-1,3 v\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=- v,\quad y=3 u v,\quad z=u.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle -3,9 u v,2 u^{2}\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(-3)(- 3 u) \\ &=9 u \\ T_{2}&=(9 u v)(-1) \\ &=- 9 u v \\ T_{3}&=(2 u^{2})(3 v) \\ &=6 u^{2} v\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=6 u^{2} v- 9 u v \\ &\quad {}+9 u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=3 u^{2} v^{2}- \frac{9 u v^{2}}{2} \\ &\quad {}+9 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=24 u^{2}- 18 u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=8 u^{3}- 9 u^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{0}^{2}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=0}^{u=2} \\ &=28.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.
